svg.title: Template rendering matrix, every Copier answer renders the expected project: the default render is canonical, and each answer changes exactly what it promises
svg.text: Template rendering matrix, every Copier answer renders
Scenario: the default render is canonical, and each answer changes exactly what it promises
What the default project looks like on GitLab
Each answer changes exactly what it promises, one branch per answer

g.text: Given GitLab holds a project rendered with every default Copier answer on its main branch
The working-branch template rendered with every default answer, then pushed as the main branch of a new GitLab project.
GitLab shows the answers file Copier wrote: container_runtime: docker, use_docker_compose: true, ansible_enabled: false,
ci_platform: gitlab_saas, gherkin_language: en.
The project's random name shows as "project", and dates and avatars are hidden, so the picture is the same on every run.
Then the main branch carries the project workspace and leaves the toolbox README out
The repository page of the main branch. The project folder sits next to .agent, .config, .devcontainer and docs, and the
root files run from .dockerignore to lefthook.yml.
There is no README.md between LICENSE and Taskfile.yml: the toolbox keeps its own README out of the projects it
generates.
And the storyboard engine folder on the main branch ships its own manual
The .config/codeceptjs folder on the main branch. README.md is in its list, and GitLab renders it under the list:
"Storyboard engine (.config/codeceptjs/storyboard.js)".
This is the storyboard engine's manual, the same file as in the toolbox.
Then choosing podman swaps docker-ce and compose for podman and changes nothing else
The same project rendered again with container_runtime: podman and pushed as the branch podman. GitLab's compare page
shows what that branch changes against the main branch: the Files panel lists every changed file, the diffs unfold the
telling ones.
Ten files change: the docker-ce files leave (their .gitignore moves to the podman folder), the podman files arrive and
project/docker-compose.yml is deleted. Taskfile.yml is unfolded: its docker-ce include goes, and a podman include
arrives further down.
And turning off Docker Compose only deletes the compose file
The same page for the branch no-compose. Only two files change: the answers file, where use_docker_compose turns false,
and project/docker-compose.yml, deleted.
The docker-ce files are not in the list, so they stay as they were.
And turning on Ansible only adds its config, its lint tooling and their Taskfile include
The same page for the branch ansible. Four new files arrive under .config/ansible and .config/ansible-lint, shown
folded.
The answers file turns ansible_enabled to true, and Taskfile.yml gains the ansible include.
And a self-hosted CI platform only changes the docker-in-docker variables and the runner
tags
The same page for the branch self-hosted, rendered with an empty docker host and certificate folder. Three files change.
In tags.yml the runner tags become an empty list. In variables.yml, DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker:2376 and the TLS settings
go, DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR turns empty and the BuildKit line is commented out. The answers file stays folded to leave room
for both files.
And turning off project mode deletes the project directory and every task that called into
it
The same page for the branch no-project. The answers file shows project_enabled turning false, and project/Taskfile.yml
and project/docker-compose.yml are deleted.
Eleven files that called into the project folder change too, shown folded with their line counts: the root Taskfile.yml,
the nine phase Taskfiles under .config/devsecops and the MegaLinter base config.
And turning off automerge only removes the fast-forward rule from the Renovate config
The same page for the branch automerge-off. The answers file turns devsecops_automerge to false.
In .config/renovate/config.json the toolbox rule loses its four automerge lines, "automergeStrategy": "fast-forward"
among them, and nothing else changes.
And choosing French Gherkin switches every test-writing rule and skill to French
The same page for the branch gherkin-fr. Six rules, skills and workflows under .agent change, each by one or two lines.
tests-structure.md is unfolded: features/ and pages/ now ask for fr instead of en. The answers file at the bottom shows
gherkin_language turning to fr.
